supersedes.why: That plan treated real photographs as the prerequisite for bullet generation and ordered a Phase 6A owner-truth hotfix BEFORE the bullet diagnostic. Measurement reversed both. Its matrix cases 3 and 4 were unconstructible -- Phase 6 has no asset ingestion path at all -- and running the equivalent through the verified_assets API parameter showed assets are INERT for bullets: output byte-identical with and without all seven. Building the 6A truth fix first would have encoded 'three real assets required' as the honest owner message, which is wrong twice over: assets do not gate bullets, and 6A's seven-spec taxonomy is not 6D/6E's three-name taxonomy.

defect.summary: Phase 6C's visible-copy gate read vocabulary where it claimed to read evidence.
defect.mechanism: _is_safe_copy kept [0] of KAP._classify_keyword's (verdict, concept, reason_code) and discarded the concept. It therefore asked 'does this copy mention a physical attribute?' while three separate comments in the module claimed it asked 'does this copy lean on an UNVERIFIED concept?'. Those questions have identical answers only while no fact is verified -- the condition every acceptance fixture ran under.
defect.consequence: With every product fact VERIFIED the bullet engine produced five complete bullets and Phase 6C blanked all five. FIT_SIZE_COLOR_ORDER_ACCURACY had NO missing requirements and was blanked anyway. The better the owner's evidence, the less copy survived.
defect.second_defect_found_by_auditing_the_muta: The bullet fix alone left the stage still crashing. validate_title_options rejects 'personalized'/'embroider'/'cotton'/'custom '/'monogram' unconditionally, while title_engine ADDS 'Embroidered'/'Personalized' only when their claims are VERIFIED. So write_phase6c_artifacts still raised Phase6CAssemblyError on a fully-verified workspace. This was found because a required mutant -- 'restore traceback' -- had nothing to restore.
defect.why_the_earlier_mutation_plan_could_have: The mutation set and differential were scoped to the bullet gate. Every one would have passed while write_phase6c_artifacts still aborted, producing a complete acceptance packet for a stage that could not finish. Auditing each mutant against an existing killer test BEFORE running the harness is what surfaced it.

measured_outcome.measured_on: A SYNTHETIC HERMETIC FIXTURE, not a real product. The workspace is built by the test's build_chain() with placeholder facts, and every fact is marked VERIFIED by the fixture rather than by an owner attesting to a real garment. The numbers below therefore prove the GATE behaves correctly given verified evidence; they do NOT prove a real listing.
measured_outcome.not_yet_measured: The same run against a real non-T2 workspace with fresh Helium 10 exports and the owner's own verified facts. That is the pilot, and it has not run. Until it does, '4 of 5 bullets' is a statement about the code path, not about any product.
measured_outcome.remaining_empty_bullet: EMBROIDERY_OR_DECORATION_PROOF - blocked inside bullet_engine.JOB_CONCEPTS, not by this gate; see boundaries
measured_outcome.corroborating_non_fixture_observation: The same 0-bullet starting condition was independently observed on a throwaway CLONE of the real runs/T2 workspace during recon, using the owner's actual keyword source. That established the defect on real data. The post-fix 4-of-5 figure was not re-measured there, because runs/T2 is quarantined and must not be used for live guidance.

design.gated_concepts: Enumerates EVERY gated concept in lexicon order, reusing the Phase 6B classifier's own vocabulary and tokeniser rather than copying them, so a lexicon edit cannot leave this gate reading a stale word list. _classify_keyword returns only the highest-ranked hit; a gate built on it verifies that one concept and publishes copy whose second, unverified concept was never examined.
design.copy_gate: Each concept is checked against its OWN claim via product_workspace._concept_verified -- the existing authority; this module never decides what 'verified' means. No import cycle: product_detail_page already imported product_workspace.
design.surfaces: Surface policy is evaluated separately from evidence. TITLE = market identity only, any gated concept blocks whatever the evidence says. BODY = bullets and highlights, where a verified concept may be stated. Without this separation, making bullets evidence-aware would have silently reversed the owner's pure-identity title decision at the title call site.
design.structured_blocks: A blocked bullet carries blocking_concepts: [{concept, reason_code, evidence_state, next_action}]. 'CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MISSING' is not something an owner can act on.

unknown_token_contract.position: INHERITED, NOT REDEFINED. gated_concepts' fallthrough to (None, EXC_PRODUCT_FACT_UNKNOWN) is deliberately identical to _classify_keyword's own final return. Narrowing it inside 6C would make this stage strictly MORE PERMISSIVE than the Phase 6B authority it borrows the entire vocabulary from -- a divergence, not a fix.

unknown_token_contract.conclusion: The feared over-block does not occur: the differentiator vocabulary claims quality adjectives before the fallthrough can. overlap_policy.policy: ALL (intersection) - both claims must be VERIFIED before such copy publishes
overlap_policy.status: EXPLICIT AND CONSERVATIVE, not an accidental consequence of duplicate vocabulary membership. Pinned by test_monogram_needs_both_of_its_concepts_verified and by mutant M2+M7(b).
overlap_policy.future: A later vocabulary-policy review may decide some overlapping terms warrant ANY or a dedicated compound concept. Deliberately not redesigned here.

title_surface_policy.rule: TITLE accepts components {identity, audience, brand}. decoration, personalization and differentiator stay out even when VERIFIED.
title_surface_policy.rationale: A policy about the field, not a judgement about the evidence. The same attributes are carried by bullets, A+ and backend terms once the BODY surface admits them.
title_surface_policy.consequence: No controlled term can reach a title, so validate_title_options' blacklist becomes a backstop that must never fire in production.
title_surface_policy.commercial_disclosure: The A_CORE keyword 'personalized nurse sweatshirt' therefore stays out of the title and lives in backend terms. This is unchanged from the pre-fix behaviour -- the fix does not make it worse -- but it is a real ranking trade-off the owner chose explicitly.

backstop_observability.problem: Under the pure-identity filter, production title assembly can never reach the controlled-term blacklist. A mutant disabling it would have survived every other test in the file. An unexercised backstop is indistinguishable from dead code -- the exact defect this project already found in Phase 6D's uncalled _is_safe_copy.
backstop_observability.solution: test_the_term_blacklist_backstop_still_fires_when_reached constructs a forbidden candidate INSIDE the test, without weakening production filtering, and asserts the validator returns a structured error list rather than raising. test_production_titles_never_reach_the_backstop asserts the complement.
backstop_observability.mutant: M4 disables the blacklist and is killed.
